flowers.name: Rose
flowers.description: Roses have a rich symbolic history. Their meaning can change significantly depending on their color and cultural context.
flowers.western: Red roses are strongly associated with romantic love. Pink roses often express admiration and gratitude, white roses can represent remembrance or new beginnings, and yellow roses are frequently associated with friendship.
flowers.eastern: In Chinese traditions, red is commonly associated with good fortune and celebration. Roses may communicate affection and beauty, but their meaning depends on the occasion and local customs.

flowers.name: Tulip
flowers.description: Tulips are elegant spring flowers often associated with affection, hope, and fresh beginnings.
flowers.western: Red tulips are associated with romantic love, while yellow varieties are often connected with cheerful thoughts and friendship.
flowers.eastern: Tulips are admired in several Asian floral traditions for their beauty and elegance. Their symbolism varies by region and is not governed by one universal meaning.

flowers.name: Peony
flowers.description: Peonies are full, expressive blooms associated with abundance, affection, and celebration.
flowers.western: Peonies are popular in wedding arrangements and may symbolize romance, prosperity, and a happy life together.
flowers.eastern: In Chinese cultural traditions, the peony is an important symbol of wealth, honor, prosperity, and beauty. It is sometimes described as the king of flowers.

flowers.name: Sunflower
flowers.description: Sunflowers are known for their bright appearance and are often used to express warmth and optimism.
flowers.western: Sunflowers commonly represent happiness, loyalty, admiration, and friendship.
flowers.eastern: Sunflowers can be associated with vitality, optimism, and positive energy. Interpretations vary among countries and traditions.

flowers.name: Daisy
flowers.description: Daisies are cheerful flowers often connected with innocence and the beauty of simple things.
flowers.western: White daisies are commonly associated with innocence and purity, while colorful varieties can suggest happiness and affection.
flowers.eastern: Daisies may be appreciated for their freshness and simplicity, although their traditional meanings differ across Asian cultures.

flowers.name: Lily
flowers.description: Lilies come in many colors and varieties. Their symbolism can shift from purity and remembrance to confidence and joy.
flowers.western: White lilies are associated with purity and are often used in religious ceremonies and remembrance. Pink lilies may express admiration, orange lilies confidence, and yellow lilies joy.
flowers.eastern: In Chinese traditions, lilies can be associated with harmony and happy unions. Some varieties are connected with wishes for lasting relationships and family happiness.

flowers.name: Lavender
flowers.description: Lavender is valued for its fragrance, delicate appearance, and association with peaceful surroundings.
flowers.western: Lavender is often connected with calmness, relaxation, grace, and devotion.
flowers.eastern: Lavender may be used to evoke serenity and balance in contemporary floral arrangements, but these associations are not universal traditional meanings across Asia.

flowers.name: Orchid
flowers.description: Orchids are admired for their distinctive shapes and extraordinary diversity of colors and species.
flowers.western: Orchids often symbolize elegance, beauty, luxury, and admiration. Purple orchids can evoke royalty, while pink varieties are often given as affectionate gifts.
flowers.eastern: In Chinese traditions, orchids can represent refinement, integrity, scholarly virtue, and noble character.

flowers.name: Carnation
flowers.description: Carnations are long-lasting flowers with meanings that depend strongly on their color and the context in which they are given.
flowers.western: Pink carnations can express gratitude and affection, red carnations admiration, white carnations remembrance or good wishes, and yellow carnations may communicate disappointment in some traditions.
flowers.eastern: Carnations are used in many contemporary Asian floral arrangements. Their meaning depends on local customs, color associations, and the occasion.

flowers.name: Iris
flowers.description: Irises have striking petals and are often chosen for messages of hope, confidence, and admiration.
flowers.western: Irises are frequently associated with wisdom, hope, faith, and courage. Purple varieties can evoke wisdom and dignity.
flowers.eastern: In Japanese traditions, iris varieties have associations with seasonal celebrations and protection. Their symbolism depends on the specific species and custom.

flowers.name: Chrysanthemum
flowers.description: Chrysanthemums have important cultural associations, and their meaning can differ considerably between countries.
flowers.western: Chrysanthemums may symbolize joy and longevity, but in some European traditions they are strongly associated with mourning and remembrance.
flowers.eastern: In China, chrysanthemums can symbolize longevity and autumn. In Japan, they are associated with the imperial family and are important symbols of the season.

flowers.name: Hydrangea
flowers.description: Hydrangeas grow in rounded clusters, and some varieties can change flower color depending on soil conditions.
flowers.western: Hydrangeas can express gratitude and heartfelt emotion. In some historical interpretations, they have also been associated with pride or boastfulness.
flowers.eastern: In Japanese cultural traditions, hydrangeas are associated with the rainy season and can be used to communicate gratitude and heartfelt feeling.

flowers.name: Gardenia
flowers.description: Gardenias are fragrant flowers known for their creamy petals and elegant appearance.
flowers.western: Gardenias can symbolize purity, grace, and secret admiration, making them a thoughtful choice for romantic gestures.
flowers.eastern: Gardenias are valued in several Asian traditions for their fragrance and beauty. Their symbolic associations vary by region and context.

flowers.name: Forget-Me-Not
flowers.description: Forget-me-nots are small flowers traditionally connected with memory, loyalty, and lasting bonds.
flowers.western: Forget-me-nots are widely associated with remembrance, enduring love, and the promise not to forget someone.
flowers.eastern: Their use in Asian floral arrangements can communicate affection and remembrance, although they do not have one shared symbolic meaning throughout Asia.

flowers.name: Lily of the Valley
flowers.description: Lily of the valley is known for its small bell-shaped flowers and delicate fragrance.
flowers.western: It is often associated with humility, happiness, and the return of joy. It is also used in some bridal bouquets.
flowers.eastern: Its meanings are less standardized across Asian traditions. It can be appreciated for its delicate appearance and fragrance.

flowers.name: Marigold
flowers.description: Marigolds are bright flowers that play important roles in celebrations and commemorative traditions.
flowers.western: Marigolds can suggest warmth and creativity, but they are also associated with remembrance and mourning in some traditions.
flowers.eastern: In parts of South Asia, marigolds are important in religious ceremonies, festivals, and wedding decorations. Their meaning depends on the specific cultural context.

flowers.name: Anemone
flowers.description: Anemones are recognizable by their delicate petals and contrasting centers.
flowers.western: In some floral traditions, anemones represent anticipation, protection, or the fragility of life.
flowers.eastern: Their symbolism varies across Asian cultures. They are often appreciated for their striking appearance in modern arrangements.
